text: Q.50 . In which month is the InterTropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) located around 20°N-25°N latitude (over the Gangetic plain) ? (a) May (b) August (c) June (d) July Sol.50.(d) July. The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a low pressure zone located at the equator where trade winds converge, and so, it is a zone where air tends to ascend. The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone located around 20°N-25°N latitudes (over the Gangetic plain) in July month is sometimes called the monsoon trough.

Q.74 . Which of the following is NOT a part of the ocean floor? (a) The continental shelf (b) The continental slope (c) The deep sea shelf (d) The deep sea plain Sol.74.(c) The deep sea shelf. A continental shelf is the submerged edge of a continent beneath the ocean. The continental slope extends seaward from the shelf to the upper edge of a continental rise or the point where the slope begins to flatten. An abyssal plain, or deep sea plain, is a flat region on the ocean floor, typically found at depths between 3,000 and 6,000 meters. Oceanic deeps are the deepest parts of the ocean, covered with fine-grained sediments such as clay and silt. Examples of oceanic landforms : Abyssal plains, Submarine canyons, Deep ocean trenches, Guyots, Seamounts, Mid-ocean ridges, Abyssal plains, etc.

Q.188 . Which of the following rivers does NOT flow in Kerala State? (a) Bharathapuzha (b) Periyar (c) Pamba (d) Penner Sol.188.(d) Penner - It rises in Nandi Hills in Chikballapur District of Karnataka and falls into the Bay of Bengal. Bharathapuzha (Ponnani) river is Kerala's second longest West Flowing River, draining into the Arabian Sea.

Q.189 . A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel is known as: (a) whorl (b) esker (c) lop (d) arch Sol.189.(b) Esker. These are ridges made of sands and gravels, deposited by glacial meltwater flowing through tunnels within and underneath glaciers, or through meltwater channels on top of glaciers. Other depositional landforms: Drumlins are smooth oval shaped ridge -like features composed mainly of glacial till with some masses of gravel and sand.

Q.296 . Peat coal has ____ carbon and ____ moisture content? (a) High, Low (b) Low, high (c) High, High (d) Low, Low Sol.296.(b) Low, high. Peat is a soft, dark brown coal that is formed from dead and decaying organic matter. It has an energy density of 15 MJ/kg. It has a low heating capacity. India has the fifth-largest coal reserves in the world. Coal India Limited (CIL) (Public Sector Undertaking) was established on 1 November 1975 under the ownership of the Ministry of Coal. Headquarters: Kolkata.

Q.314 . What was the main objective of the Second Green Revolution in India? (a) Ensuring food security in the western states (b) Promoting conventional agricultural practices (c) Focusing on holistic development in agriculture (d) Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides Sol.314.(c) In the second phase of the green revolution (mid-1970s to mid-1980s), the HYV technology spread to a larger number of states and benefited more variety of crops. The spread of green revolution technology enabled India to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains.

Q.406 . Sundari trees are found in which type of forests in India? (a) Mangrove forests (b) Tropical deciduous forests (c) The thorn forests and scrubs (d) Tropical evergreen forests Sol.406.(a) Mangrove forests. Sundari tree is the most abundant tree in the mangrove forests of the Sunderban delta in West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Sunderbans are named after the Sundari tree. Mangrove forests grow only at tropical and subtropical latitudes near the equator because they cannot withstand freezing temperatures. Uppu ponna, Boddu ponna, Urada, Mada, Telli Mada, Gundu mada, Kadili, Palm, coconut, keora, agar and Bella are some of the typical vegetation of the mangroves.

Q.438 . Which of the following trees will you find in the Littoral forests? (a) Chinar (b) Ebony (c) Sundari (d) Cypress Sol.438.(c) Sundari tree is found in Sundarbans delta in West Bengal in Mangrove forest (Littoral forests). Climate

Q.489 . Which of the following pressure belts is known as the horse latitude? (a) Equatorial Low Pressure (b) Sub - Polar Low Pressure (c) High Pressure (d) Sub - Tropical High Pressure Sol.489.(d) Subtropical high pressure belts (Horse latitude) extend 30° N and 30° S. It is formed because the warm air rising from the equator moves towards the tropics in both hemispheres. Equatorial Low - Pressure belt extends from 0 to 5° North and South. The subpolar low pressure belt extends around latitudes 60° to 70° North and South. High Pressure belts are located at 70°- 90° North and South latitudes. There are majorly seven Pressure Belts on the surface of Earth i.e., the Equatorial Low, two Subtropical Highs, two Subpolar Lows, and two Polar Highs.

Q.613 . As of Financial year 2019, which of the following states has the highest road density in India? (a) Haryana (b) Tamil Nadu (c) Kerala (d) Punjab Sol.613.(c) Kerala. As of the financial year 2019, Kerala had the highest road density among states, with 6.7 thousand kilometers of roads per one thousand square kilometers. Among union territories, Chandigarh had the highest road density in India, with over 22.6 thousand kilometers per one thousand square kilometers. Road density refers to the total length of all roads in a country, including highways, national roads, and city or rural roads, compared to the country's land area.

Q.766 . The upper portion of the earth is known as: (a) Stratosphere (b) Troposphere (c) Lithosphere (d) Mesosphere Sol.766.(c) Lithosphere. It is bounded by the atmosphere above and the asthenosphere (another part of the upper mantle) below. The stratosphere is the second-lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere. The troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere, contains about 75-80% of the atmospheric mass. Most clouds form in the troposphere, where nearly all weather occurs. The mesosphere is the third highest layer, situated between the stratosphere and the thermosphere.

Q.802 . Name an oval-shaped range of hills sculpted by glacial flow. (a) Sandur (b) Drumlins (c) Moraines (d) Esker Sol.802.(b) Drumlins - It is formed by the filling of heavy rocky debris in the glacial crevices and its stay under the ice. One end of the drumlins facing the glacier called the stoss end and the other end called tail. Eskers: When glaciers melt in summer, the water flows on the surface of the ice. These waters accumulate beneath the glacier and flow like streams in a channel beneath the ice.

Q.838 . Which of the following statements is best related to the 'pacific ring of fire'? (a) Known for thermal power station (b) Known for volcano and earthquakes (c) Known for only glacial formations (d) Known for tropical rainforests Sol.838.(b) The 'ring of fire' is a ring of volcanoes in the Pacific Ocean. Q.915 . ___________species are the species which are not found after searches of known or likely areas where they may occur. (a) Extinct (b) Endangered (c) Normal (d) Vulnerable Sol.915.(a) Extinct. An endangered species is a type of organism that is threatened by extinction. Examples: Black Rhino, Tiger, Whale, Red Panda, Chimpanzee, Asian Elephant etc.
